levels.VALIDATED: Deterministic rule reproducing its field exactly (≥ 99.999% of rows) on every split, or a parameter whose 95% CI contains the theoretical value and which passes on all 5 splits with an independent second implementation / out-of-sample test.
levels.STRONGLY SUPPORTED: Validator passes on all 5 splits with a wide margin; mechanism specified explicitly; best alternative tested and rejected.
levels.SUPPORTED: Validator passes, but part of the mechanism is inferred, thresholds are analyst-chosen, or the rule rests on one evidence line.
levels.CANDIDATE: Pattern detected and replicated, mechanism not yet formulated as a testable rule.
levels.INCONCLUSIVE: Dependence or effect established but the generating mechanism is not identified, or the result is a documented negative (no signature found).
levels.REJECTED: Hypothesis tested and contradicted by the data (kept for transparency).

rules.title: PARTICIPANT_COUNT = number of known BICs in BIC8_PATH
rules.hypothesis: PARTICIPANT_COUNT is derived from the path, not drawn independently.
rules.method: Exact equality test on all rows; pure-Python re-implementation on 200k sample.
rules.counterexamples: None found.
rules.limitations: Says nothing about how many hops were hidden.
rules.economic: Counts observed institutions only, i.e. what the messaging layer can see.
rules.formulation: PARTICIPANT_COUNT := number of BIC8 entries in BIC8_PATH that are not '...'
rules.logic: pc = |{b ∈ split(path,';') : b ≠ '...'}|  · rulelib.participant_count

rules.method: Exact equivalence test.
rules.counterexamples: None.
rules.limitations: Flag is an observability marker, not payment success/failure.

rules.title: Path endpoints differ from ORDERING/BENEFICIARY_BIC8 independently with p≈0.05 each
rules.criterion: first & last mismatch in [0.045,0.055] and joint/product ratio in [0.9,1.1]

rules.method: Mismatch rates per end, joint vs product (independence), stratified by type, pc, anomaly.
rules.counterexamples: ROMANCE_SCAM never swaps; CEO/ACCOUNT_REPLACEMENT never swap at the beneficiary end (mule bank is the true receiver).
rules.limitations: Cannot tell which institution is 'real' from one field alone; R5b resolves it with currency/clock/IBAN evidence.

rules.formulation: With probability 0.05 the first known path BIC is replaced by another bank; independently, with probability 0.05 the last known BIC is replaced

rules.title: Intermediaries K = floor(Exp(1)): P(K=k) = (1-1/e)e^-k
rules.criterion: MLE continuation q within ±0.005 of 1/e and Cohen's w < 0.01 on every split
rules.hypothesis: Number of intermediaries follows a simple distribution.
rules.method: Geometric MLE, successive ratios, chi-square GOF with Cohen's w, per split; per-bank Direct share vs binomial.
rules.counterexamples: None beyond sampling noise. Max pc = 22 is the far tail: the rule predicts 10M·e^-15 ≈ 3.1 rows with pc ≥ 17; 5 are observed (Poisson P(X≥5 | 3.1) ≈ 0.2).
rules.limitations: Correspondent choice is random in the generator; real networks depend on bilateral relationships.
rules.economic: Each extra correspondent hop is a fixed-probability event; most payments have a direct relationship.
rules.formulation: Number of intermediaries K ~ ⌊Exp(1)⌋; PARTICIPANT_COUNT = K + 2
rules.logic: P(K = k) = (1 − e⁻¹)·e⁻ᵏ; MLE q̂ = K̄/(1+K̄); GOF χ² → Cohen's w
rules.validation: PASS on 5 splits (P1, P2, full, half_0, half_1)

violation.text: None beyond sampling noise. Max pc = 22 is the far tail: the rule predicts 10M·e^-15 ≈ 3.1 rows with pc ≥ 17; 5 are observed (Poisson P(X≥5 | 3.1) ≈ 0.2).

rules.alternative: Poisson hop counts (successive ratios not constant)

rules.title: Covered vs Indirect is a per-sending-bank propensity (cover-prone banks ≈61%, others ≈7%, out of sample), independent of route length

rules.formulation: Among non-direct routes, TRANSACTION_TYPE = Covered with a sending-bank propensity π_b (cover banks π ≈ 0.6–0.8, others π ≈ 0.05); independent of K
rules.logic: π_b estimated on half 0; Covered share on half 1 by class; Cramér's V(type × K)
rules.validation: PASS on 5 splits (P1, P2, full, half_0, half_1)

rules.title: FX count = adjacent known-BIC pairs with different home currencies
rules.hypothesis: FX count is deterministic in the route.
rules.method: Exact rule test on all rows; two rejected alternatives; pure-Python cross-check.
rules.counterexamples: 2 rows, and they are the only 2 payments in the dataset that touch an Eritrean bank (0000ERA0, receiver). Eritrea never sends, so its home currency cannot be inferred and the rule's input is unobservable there; if ER's currency differs from the sender's, C2 predicts exactly the recorded 1 conversion. Scope: C2 holds wherever every route country has an observable home currency.
rules.limitations: Home currency per country is inferred from the data (modal currency).

rules.title: Payment currency is drawn from the currencies on the route: first bank ≈ 95% (direct), receiver bank ≈ 3.8%, +≈2.4 pts per intermediary, outside-route vehicle ≈ 1.3%
rules.criterion: ≥98% of payments in a route-bank currency on every split; receiver-only share stable across route lengths (range < 0.006); intermediary-only share rises ≈ linearly per intermediary (slope 0.02–0.035)
rules.hypothesis: Where the payment currency comes from.
rules.method: Currency matched against the home currencies of every bank on the path, by route length; per split on a 3M-row reservoir sample.
rules.counterexamples: 1.27% of payments (126,857) use a currency of no route bank; 77.7% of them are EUR or USD. H38 (all 10M rows, 5 splits): on routes with no EUR or USD bank the payment is in EUR 1.41% and USD 0.75% of the time, stable across route length (pc 2–5) and splits (EUR 1.39–1.42%) — a route-independent vehicle draw that shows up as 'outside' only when that currency is not already on the route. Supported refinement, not a separate validated rule (the EUR/USD set was chosen after inspection).

rules.validation: PASS on 5 splits (P1, P2, full, half_0, half_1)

rules.alternative: currency chosen before routing (cannot be excluded; route-first is the more parsimonious reading)

rules.title: Intermediaries drawn i.i.d. with replacement ∝ bank size — predicts the path revisit (loop) rate
